new_symbol_range_suggestions.velocity_damping_saturation_scale: positive, with units of velocity squared; large compared with typical v**2 recovers nearly linear damping, while values comparable to early-time v**2 reveal measurable drag-law curvature

derivation_notes: The parent assumed viscous damping remained exactly proportional to velocity even when the delayed anharmonic damping channel was strongly active. Here the same effective damping strength multiplies an odd saturating velocity law v/sqrt(1 + v**2/velocity_damping_saturation_scale), which preserves linear damping for small |v| and yields weaker incremental deceleration at larger |v| due to finite-rate scattering into bath modes.
change_summary: Relaxed the assumption of globally linear friction by introducing a velocity-saturation scale in the damping law while leaving the restoring-force and delayed activation state y unchanged. This directly changes the scored dv_dt mapping through curvature in its dependence on v at fixed Q and y.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Damping is linear in the phonon velocity for all post-preparation excursions.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Finite-rate anharmonic scattering into bath modes can make the effective friction law sublinear at high instantaneous phonon velocity, while still remaining odd in v and strictly dissipative.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: For velocity_damping_saturation_scale much larger than all observed v**2, sqrt(1 + v**2/velocity_damping_saturation_scale) approaches 1 and the parent damping law is recovered.

response_change.parent_relation: The damping contribution to dv_dt is linear in v with an effective coefficient damping_rate + amplitude_dependent_damping*y, so at fixed Q and y the target changes with a single constant slope in v.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the linear viscous damping assumption by a velocity-saturating dissipative law so that, at fixed Q and y, the damping-induced part of dv_dt remains odd and opposing motion but its slope with respect to v decreases at larger |v|.
response_change.observable_effect: Large-amplitude ringdown segments with high velocity show weaker-than-linear additional deceleration versus |v|, while small-velocity late-time dynamics remain close to the parent linear damping behavior.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories reach a regime with substantial delayed damping activation y and sufficiently large |v| during early or intermediate ringdown, while remaining in the post-preparation undriven decay scenario.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate excursions can reveal nearly linear damping near v≈0 and the onset of drag-law bending at larger |v|; in holdout, stronger initial oscillations extend the same monotone curvature change without introducing a different mechanism.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the velocity-saturation scale is large compared with all observed |v|, so the damping law reduces to the existing linear-in-v form.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: velocity-saturating phonon friction under delayed anharmonic bath coupling
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Finite-rate anharmonic scattering into bath modes can make the effective friction law sublinear at high instantaneous phonon velocity, while still remaining odd in v and strictly dissipative.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because the damping coefficient and velocity are first combined and then passed through a nonlinear saturation map, creating a fixed-Q,fixed-y curvature in dv_dt versus v that no single linear gain can match across both small- and large-|v| regimes.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: Damping is linear in the phonon velocity for all post-preparation excursions.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The damping channel remains odd and dissipative but crosses over from linear viscous behavior to sublinear velocity saturation at high |v|.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: For velocity_damping_saturation_scale much larger than all observed v**2, the denominator sqrt(1 + v**2/velocity_damping_saturation_scale) tends to 1 and the exact parent expression is recovered.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: At matched Q and y, dv_dt as a function of v is no longer a straight line: near v=0 it has the parent's slope, but at larger |v| the damping contribution bends toward smaller magnitude than linear prediction. This contrast is observable in early high-speed versus late low-speed portions of the same ringdown trajectory when y has become appreciable.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the near-origin linear slope and the reduced large-|v| slope across those conditions, because once Q and y are specified the parent dependence on v is exactly linear with one constant slope. Adjusting damping_rate or amplitude_dependent_damping only rescales that line and cannot create the required curvature.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when trajectories reach a regime with substantial delayed damping activation y and sufficiently large |v| during early or intermediate ringdown, while remaining in the post-preparation undriven decay scenario.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate excursions can reveal nearly linear damping near v≈0 and the onset of drag-law bending at larger |v|; in holdout, stronger initial oscillations extend the same monotone curvature change without introducing a different mechanism.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit where the velocity-saturation scale is large compared with all observed |v|, so the damping law reduces to the existing linear-in-v form.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes the dissipative force is exactly proportional to velocity even when the anharmonically activated decay channel is strongly engaged, omitting plausible saturation of frictional energy transfer at high phonon speed.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Damping is linear in the phonon velocity for all post-preparation excursions.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite-rate anharmonic scattering into bath modes can make the effective friction law sublinear at high instantaneous phonon velocity, while still remaining odd in v and strictly dissipative.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's globally linear damping assumption rather than add a new process. The parent target mapping is dv_dt = restoring(Q) minus an effective damping coefficient times v, so for fixed Q and y every v-slice is a straight line with one slope. That is a single-gain shortcut. A scientifically natural child keeps the same delayed damping state y and the same restoring-force structure, but changes the damping law so the target's dependence on v bends at larger speed. The varied condition is the accessible velocity magnitude along trajectories, especially comparing early high-speed oscillation segments against late low-speed segments, while material parameters and the post-preparation environment are held fixed across each trajectory. Under admissible strong-preparation conditions, y can be appreciable and |v| can transiently be large; then the child predicts weaker incremental deceleration per added speed than the parent. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce both the near-origin linear slope and the reduced large-|v| slope across those conditions, because its v-dependence is exactly linear once Q and y are specified. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. The limitation is that if all observed trajectories stay in a small-|v| regime, the refinement becomes hard to distinguish and effectively collapses back to the parent.

scenario_text: Track a coherent optical-phonon coordinate after a crystal is displaced from its equilibrium lattice configuration. The coordinate and its velocity evolve jointly through lattice inertia, harmonic restoring forces, and damping into other vibrational modes. Material coefficients and the post-preparation environment remain fixed along each trajectory. The regression target is the acceleration of the phonon coordinate.
